title: Vector query capacity degeneration and reranker drift postmortem
creator: Priya Shah
description: Incident affecting the embeddings + rerank API: customers observed degraded recall and a spike in 95th percentile latency for vector queries. This postmortem covers detection, root cause analysis, mitigations applied during the incident, and longer-term remediation to prevent recurrence.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~02:25 UTC we began seeing increased error rates and latency for the /v1/rerank endpoint for several customers. Over the next hour throughput dropped on several GPU worker pools as pods entered a crash-restart loop and a fallback reranker model was invoked for some requests. Simultaneously we observed a quality regression in top-K recall for a subset of requests after a model binary rollout. The incident lasted ~5 hours for full resolution; partial mitigations reduced customer impact within 45 minutes.
impact:
- Elevated 95p latency from ~120ms to ~1.2s for rerank requests across eu-west-1 and us-west-2 for ~4 hours.
- Measured reduction in top-3 recall for the primary reranker by ~12% on production evaluation prompts after a model variant rollout.
- Approximately 17% of customer requests hit the degraded fallback path (lower-quality reranker) during the incident window.
- Several enterprise customers reported increased error rates affecting search features; two customers opened high-priority tickets.
detection: Alert channel: SLO-alert-rerank-95p triggered at 02:28 UTC. Pager duty paged on-call infra and rerank owners. Internal customer support escalations began at 02:34 UTC. Automated canary comparisons showed a widening quality delta at 02:40 UTC between canary and stable reranker buckets.
timeline:
- 02:25 UTC: First SLO noise; monitoring shows 95p latency rising.
- 02:28 UTC: SLO-alert-rerank-95p fires.
- 02:34 UTC: Customer support tickets for search flakiness begin.
- 02:40 UTC: Canary evaluation pipeline reports quality regression for reranker variant v3.1.
- 02:50 UTC: Autoscaler started aggressively terminating and recreating GPU pods in eu-west-1 due to a faulty termination notification handler (OOM signal misinterpreted as healthy).
- 03:05 UTC: Engineering disabled reranker v3.1 rollout and rolled back to v3.0.
- 03:15 UTC: Temporary traffic routing to fallback capacity pool (dedicated warm pool) for highest priority customers.
- 03:50 UTC: Applied a hotfix to the termination handler to stop flapping pods; warm pool stabilized latency.
- 06:00 UTC: Full service metrics returned to baseline; quality checks validated recall restored to within acceptable thresholds.
- 06:15 UTC: Post-incident customer outreach started; incident report shared with affected accounts.
root_cause: Two independent failures coincided and amplified impact: (1) a model rollout (reranker v3.1) contained a preprocessing tokenizer change that produced shifted embedding vectors for edge-case inputs, producing a measurable recall regression. (2) An autoscaler termination-healthcheck regression (introduced in autoscaler v1.14) caused GPU pods to be killed and recreated under load rather than gracefully draining, creating cache churn and transient OOMs which increased latency and reduced capacity.
contributing_factors:
- Canary tests lacked a specific slice of real-world prompt patterns (long-chained context prompts) where the tokenizer change mattered.
- Autoscaler health-check change removed a small sleep/drain that previously allowed KV cache eviction to complete; this increased cache misses and GPU memory pressure.
- Release process allowed v3.1 to be promoted from canary to gradual rollout before full slice coverage.
- Monitoring thresholds for pod restart rate were low-sensitivity and didn't automatically pause rollouts.
- No automated e2e rerank quality gate for top-K recall in the deployment pipeline.
immediate_mitigation:
- Rolled back reranker to v3.0 within 35 minutes of detection.
- Reconfigured autoscaler to use the previous termination behavior and increased drain timeout, preventing further pod flapping.
- Shifted high-priority customer traffic to warm pool instances with pre-warmed KV caches.
- Enabled temporary rate limiting for non-critical backgrounds rerank jobs to reduce pressure on GPU pools.
long_term_remediation:
- Add a dedicated 'long-context' test slice to canary evaluation covering tokenizer edge-cases and long-chain prompts.
- Implement a top-K recall quality gate (automated) that blocks rollouts if regression > 3% on production-like prompt sets.
- Revert and fix autoscaler termination logic; add a unit and integration test ensuring graceful KV cache drain on termination.
- Introduce an autoscaler rollback circuit breaker: if restart rate > X within Y minutes, pause rollouts and notify owners.
- Create a warm-pool autoscaling policy to keep a small number of GPU pods always pre-warmed with KV caches for low-latency failover.
- Update runbooks and SLO alerts to include combined latency+quality heuristics to surface model regressions faster.
follow_up_actions: ENG-24045: Add long-context prompt slice to canary evaluation (owner: Ava Thompson, estimate: 3)
ENG-24046: Implement top-K recall automated gate in CI/CD (owner: Marcus Li, estimate: 5)
ENG-24047: Rework autoscaler termination handler + tests (owner: Diego Martinez, estimate: 8)
ENG-24048: Warm-pool autoscaling policy prototype and rollout (owner: Priya Shah, estimate: 5)
PM-515: Communicate incident and SLA credits to affected customers (owner: Lina Ortiz, estimate: 2)
ENG-24060: Dashboard combining token latency and top-K recall trends for early detection (owner: SRE team, estimate: 3)
metrics: Top-3 recall baseline: 0.84 -> dropped to 0.74 during v3.1 rollout
Pod restart rate in eu-west-1: baseline 0.02 restarts/hour -> 3 restarts/hour during incident window
Fraction of requests hitting fallback reranker: ~17% during mitigation window
lessons_learned:
- Model rollouts must include quality gates that match production slices, not just average metrics.
- Infrastructure changes (autoscaler) that affect termination semantics must be treated as high-risk for inference services with in-memory caches; they need expanded testing.
- Warm pools materially reduce latency impact during replacement events.
- Combined alerts (latency + quality) surface issues faster than single-metric SLOs.
owner_comments: We underestimated coupling between model preprocessing and deployment semantics. The immediate rollback and autoscaler revert were effective, but investing in automated quality gates and warm-pool capability will prevent recurrence and reduce MTTA/MTTR. Marcus will drive the CI/CD quality gate work; Diego will lead the autoscaler rebuild. Priority scheduling requested in next planning cycle.
